independent_full_roster_review.text:
# Independent review: 331 current authored-use successor v1

The bounded source-review data and exact dialog-continuation owner are supported as a reviewable proposal; the **integrated production admission is not ready**. Frozen patch SHA256 `b09523eaa293e685549dc0a826291913ebbe6a8db62fb2e28680e5eb0c2c99d5`; manifest SHA256 `dfb315aa1880cce46dac8cd4f8443b0d403d22095cc28c8b21b8ad6cc00f9453`; base `931f857f13990a75d14db2b158666b51c521765d`. I applied the patch only to an isolated set of exact base images, with whitespace errors rejected: all 24 afterimages and byte counts match the manifest. The 317-row predecessor is also archived as the exact original ledger bytes, SHA256 `f511e46130f3376aadf7796365db533eaa0f35979dd99e8abffaf859d8127057`.

Independently checked exact keys and source data: 509 source files, 1,931 live peer uses, 329 additions beyond the unchanged 1,736 frozen seed, plus precisely two previously recorded retired obligations, totaling 331 unique rows. All 317 prior row objects are retained: 208 unchanged, 109 embedded whole in successor rows; 14 rows are newly added. Every one of the 329 live rows has the scanner's exact current source hash and occurrences; the two retained nonlive roles are menu `MatMenuContent` and dialog `MatDialogConfig`. There are no duplicate, orphan or unaccounted rows. All 331 selected review records exist uniquely, bind the row's source hash, and all directly enumerated review/evidence hashes match the staged or canonical bytes. The 14 new-use declaration files also match the recorded installed 22.1.7 hashes; six core records spell the version as `@angular/core 22.1.7`, while the others use `22.1.7`. Source/declaration identity does not prove behavior by itself.

The semantic assessment relies on the already independent family-level receipts and the prior individual role histories. My own 16-use and 20-use complete prior/current source diffs are embedded. The generated OverlayRef decision explicitly corrects the historical review: it is required and lacks `@Optional` in both concrete signatures. The common-module re-export changes, form-field subscript motion, select ripple signal and dialog close cancelling pending focus have their separately scoped semantics; they are not evidence that entire files remained byte-identical. V5 dialog closed-shadow timing, native nonzero results and lifecycle limits remain. New option/optgroup/select signal uses and other new roles are recorded only as scoped source judgments, not blanket runtime or peer-floor approval.

Independently ran the staged production targeted wrapper with the actual 509-file scan: direct roster evidence 331/331, 21 identity/inventory negatives, dialog owner positive and seven negatives passed. The isolated physical-drift control rejected a mutation made by the last callback and accepted restoration; I first confirmed the deliberately mutated evidence file was copy-on-write and not a canonical hardlink. An independent wrong-line control rejected all 331 for 21.x. Conversely, a deliberately false OverlayRef semantic decision with its review body rehashed was accepted (one reviewed, zero insufficient): the generic helper verifies content bindings, not semantic truth. The independent reviews and strict immutable evidence ownership remain essential.

The row file retains `status: closed` as source-review metadata and `g11_claim: not-passed`; neither denotes a successful full admission. I exercised actual `currentAuthoredUseAdmission` with the real scanner and the frozen staged 331 candidate. It reports reviewed 331/insufficient 0, but `ready=false`, `scope_valid=false`, `source_snapshot_valid=false`; from repository cwd the inherited path rejects `changed retired-role type proof adapter` before the new continuation. The predecessor raw-reader check instead rejects the historical physical repair guard planner. From outside the repository, even with explicit root, the existing old guard's Git subprocess fails due to cwd. The v1 manifest names the predecessor physical-guard failure but does not name the actual staged-adapter failure; a successor manifest should record both. These are not generic missing-file exceptions and must not be bypassed. Resolve the old guard with a separately reviewed exact source transition, then execute the actual production positive and corruption/late-mutation controls. Until then no production completion, current roster admission or protected-check pass is asserted.

The scoped dialog owner itself has separately frozen independent review `review-retirement-v2.md`, SHA256 `bc0dc36b01cca4ce11ab354ff346d17966d895468ad9540fcc9f65f9d854ec0c`. Main-only snapshot; no full frozen roster, native/floor, 21.x, security, G11 or release qualification follows. The current tree can move; integrator must recheck exact beforeimages, population and all 24 afterimages. During earlier probe preparation I briefly created and then moved an untracked probe from canonical and removed its empty directory; no tracked canonical file changed.

independent_root_forward_review.text:
# Independent review: current roster root forwarding

Forwarding patch SHA-256 `1cf1048b783679aabb951b1add532ddbf50794cef5d6f4568bfbab1325bca9c4`; manifest SHA `ffa5fb8e77d49ba4faa593d4d26b89d83345bb9a232725d93f521c53a634714c`; root-aware predecessor `current-roster-successor-v1.patch` SHA `b09523eaa293e685549dc0a826291913ebbe6a8db62fb2e28680e5eb0c2c99d5`. Caller preimages taken from `931f857f`; all work in temporary or read-only candidate sources, with no canonical edits.

No blocking finding in the bounded forwarding change. Independent production census finds 17 calls in 16 files; the 18th textual match is the API declaration. Each changed call forwards exactly its existing lexical root parameter or, in the checker, its existing module root. TypeScript symbol inspection resolved all 17 references. Removing the inserted `root,` from each output reproduced each input byte-for-byte. No branch condition, CLI flag, guard, or other production source changed. Strict patch application passed in a small source-only tree.

Replayed the proposed call-expression probe: all 17 actual extracted expressions capture the alternate root and all 18 omitted-root controls reject. This probe substitutes the downstream baseline and is not a full inspector execution. Separately executed the genuine patched scanner and API with explicit root over 509 actual files and 1,931 current uses: 331 reviewed, zero insufficient, but `ready=false`. With the repository as process cwd the existing retired-role type proof adapter reports `changed retired-role type proof adapter`; from `/tmp`, the inherited Git subprocess instead fails because it uses cwd rather than the supplied root. The previously reported historical repair-guard planner issue remains unqualified, not resealed or passed. Root forwarding alone therefore does not establish alternate-cwd production readiness.

An actual-scanner `21.x` API fixture with an explicitly supplied empty baseline produced identical implicit- and explicit-root results and remained not ready. No branch-specific logic was changed, but this fixture is not a real 21.x checkout, complete inspector, peer floor or release qualification. Existing legacy test-probe callsites were outside the 17-production-call scope; no full test or G11 pass is asserted.
